variants.name: Current settings
variants.desc: Every breakout that passes the rules is taken, with early exit on.

variants.name: No early exit
variants.desc: Same, but trades are only left at the stop-loss, target or time exit.

variants.name: With daily limits
variants.desc: Early exit on, but at most 2 trades a day per market and a stop after one loss.

verdict: After estimated costs the rules lost a net ₹17,812 over 334 trades (32.0% winners). Before costs they were ahead by ₹25,983, so trading costs took all of it. With this many trades the true win rate could plausibly be anywhere from 27.3% to 37.2%. Luck check: the same rules run on shuffled prices, which have no real pattern, did about as well before costs, so these results show no sign of a real edge.
assumptions: Option prices are estimated from the index with the Black-Scholes formula, because expired options have no price history. Real prices will differ, especially around events.
Costs deducted: ₹100 per option trade plus 0.5% slippage on each leg; ₹40 plus 0.03% of turnover and 0.03% slippage per leg on stocks.
Expiry days, strike gaps and lot sizes use today's exchange rules for every past day.
Index average-price lines are plain averages of the index, because an index has no volume. Live, the tool uses the index future.
Crude oil, gold, silver and natural gas are not in this backtest: expired commodity contracts have no history to test on.
News has no effect on trades (it is shown for information only), so it is not part of the test.
Nothing was tuned to this data. The rules, stops and filters are exactly the ones used live.
